If the same holds for supervision, context-enriched fine-tuning will not beat triple-only.

input.strongest_for: The idea targets a cell of the landscape that the retrieved literature leaves unoccupied: every analyzed high-relevance work manipulates context at inference time (SG-RAG MOT curates a frozen LLM's prompt, CLAUSE learns a context policy 'without retraining', Co-E is training-free, the answer-path study varies prompt composition), so the training-time supervision signal is a genuinely distinct, testable variable. The design is falsifiable and cheap to state: same base model, matched supervision budget, triple/path-only vs same-passage context-enriched supervision, with hop-depth breakdowns and a standard benchmark suite (MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ, Hits@1) and published baselines (EmbedKGQA, GreaseLM/MHGRN, KICGPT). The hop-transfer question (H2) is scientifically interesting independent of whether the method wins, and the repair-loop diagnostic (one-hop failure rate) would be a useful measurement even if it yields a null result.
input.strongest_against: The core premise is contradicted by the closest controlled evidence available: holding the number of triples fixed, replacing every non-answer-chain triple with material from an unrelated entity changes multi-hop answer accuracy by only +0.003 F1 (C002), while removing the answer chain costs most of the graph's value; separately, inflated context is reported to introduce distractors that depress accuracy (C003). Since the idea's intervention is precisely to add more same-passage triples beyond the target path, the most likely outcome is a null or negative effect, and the answer-path study explicitly warns that asymmetric prompt/format handling can manufacture spurious context findings (C007). Compounding this, the only RL transfer evidence is cross-formalism with a +1.7% downstream KGQA gain and no hop-depth analysis (C005), leaving H2 unsupported, and a training-free system is already competitive with trained systems (C006), so even a small positive training-time effect may not constitute a meaningful contribution. The three-component pipeline (context supervision + repair loop + low-hop RL) is also an unfocused bundle whose failure of any one part obscures the others.
input.most_important_unresolved_question: Does same-passage context change the model's learned reasoning ability (transferable to unseen deeper-hop queries), rather than merely supplying more tokens or the answer path at inference — and can this be demonstrated under a matched-token-budget, format-controlled comparison against an inference-time-context baseline?
input.most_dangerous_confounder: The context-enriched and triple-only regimes differ simultaneously in (a) token budget, (b) whether the answer path is explicitly present, (c) response format induced by the prompt, and (d) relevance of added triples. Any measured gain could be produced entirely by token budget, answer-path leakage, or format sensitivity rather than by 'supporting context' (C002, C007, C003). The design must include a matched-budget shuffled/random-context arm, identical templates except for triple content, and a format-controlled scorer; otherwise the central claim is unidentifiable.
input.closest_work_explanation: SG-RAG MOT (doi:10.20944/preprints202505.1992.v1) is conceptually closest: it builds and curates a local triple subgraph for multi-hop KGQA on MetaQA, but for a frozen LLM and with no training-regime or hop-depth comparison (C004, C008). CLAUSE (arxiv:2509.21035) also constructs a local subgraph with RL for MetaQA/HotpotQA/FactKG, but the RL trains a context-selection policy and the reader is not retrained (C001), and it reports that over-retrieval creates distractors (C003). The answer-path study (arxiv:2609.10237) is the sharpest challenge: it isolates the value of surrounding vs answer-path triples at inference and finds the former nearly irrelevant (C002) while flagging format artifacts (C007). Co-E (arxiv:2607.23278) shows a training-free graph-text context system competitive with trained systems, questioning the need for training-time supervision (C006). None of the four changes the fine-tuning supervision signal or measures shallow-to-deep hop transfer.
input.potential_contribution: If validated, the contribution is a supervision recipe plus an evidence-based boundary characterization: when does same-passage context enriched supervision help multi-hop KGQA, when does it not, and does low-hop-only RL transfer to deeper hops. Realistically the most valuable form of this contribution is a careful negative/boundary result and a reusable evaluation protocol (matched-budget shuffled-context control, format-controlled scoring, hop-depth transfer gap, one-hop failure rate), rather than a new state-of-the-art system. If the training-time effect is null and the inference-time effect is real, documenting that distinction is itself a useful clarification of the field.
input.overlap_summary: High conceptual overlap on the problem (multi-hop KGQA) and the mechanism vocabulary (local context subgraph of KG triples): SG-RAG MOT and CLAUSE both assemble/curate such subgraphs and share MetaQA; the answer-path study manipulates which triples accompany multi-hop questions; Co-E builds graph context from text. Overlap on the specific contribution (training-time supervision manipulation) is absent in the analyzed set, but the inference-time literature already occupies most of the 'context helps' claim space.
input.distinction_summary: The distinctions are (1) training-time vs inference-time manipulation of the context, (2) same-source-passage provenance of the added triples rather than KG-neighborhood retrieval, (3) an explicit one-hop failure detector/repair loop producing corrective training examples, and (4) a hop-depth transfer protocol where the model is RL-optimized only on lower-hop instances and evaluated on deeper hops. Points (1) and (4) are conceptual rather than implementation-level; points (2) and (3) are currently under-specified and may reduce to existing KG-neighborhood augmentation and generic iterative self-training if not formalized precisely.

novelty.finding: No directly matching work was found in the searched literature: the retrieved/analyzed context-construction works are inference-time or architecture-level. This is a literature search result, not proof of novelty; searches were limited to the recorded queries and 83 retrieved papers.
novelty.question: Has essentially the same idea been proposed before?

novelty.finding: The training-vs-inference distinction is conceptual, not merely implementation-level, so the idea is not just a re-implementation. However, if an inference-time context baseline at matched budget matches the context-enriched model, the distinction collapses into an empirical comparison rather than a new capability (C009).
novelty.question: Is the difference only implementation-level?

technical_validity.finding: The mechanism assumes surrounding same-passage triples carry learnable signal, but the closest controlled evidence finds non-answer-path triples change multi-hop accuracy by +0.003 F1 at inference. The training-time analogue is untested, so H1 is at high risk of a null effect.
technical_validity.question: Is the mechanism plausible - does surrounding context carry learnable signal?

technical_validity.finding: Adding triples risks adding distractors; the literature explicitly reports over-retrieval depressing accuracy and recommends compact curated context, so the intervention direction may be wrong unless relevance-filtered.
technical_validity.question: Could enrichment actively harm accuracy?

technical_validity.finding: The adaptive repair loop is under-specified: no retrieved work defines or validates automated one-hop failure detection and corrective example generation for KGQA, so this component is an untested assumption (C011).
technical_validity.question: Is the repair loop technically defined and distinct from generic iterative self-training?

experimental_validity.finding: Token budget, answer-path presence, and response format differ between the two regimes and can produce the claimed result without any effect of supporting context. Without a matched-budget shuffled-context arm, identical templates, and a format-controlled scorer, H1 is not identifiable.
experimental_validity.question: What confounders could produce the claimed result?

experimental_validity.finding: The planned baselines (triple-only fine-tuning, EmbedKGQA, GreaseLM, KICGPT) do not include a training-free inference-time context baseline (e.g., Co-E-style or GraphRAG-style prompting at matched budget), which is the actual competitor for the 'context helps' claim.
experimental_validity.question: Are baselines strong and budgets matched?

experimental_validity.finding: The hop-transfer protocol (H2) has no established precedent or measurement convention in the retrieved set; without pre-registered hop-depth splits and a construction analysis, transfer may be an artifact of how MetaQA 3-hop is built.
experimental_validity.question: Does the evaluation actually test transfer?

practicality.finding: The intervention requires same-passage triple alignments that are unverified for MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ; MetaQA is not passage-aligned, so the mechanism may have to be redefined as KG-neighborhood context, which weakens the novel claim (C010).
practicality.question: Is the same-passage mechanism implementable on the chosen benchmarks?

practicality.finding: The full pipeline requires LoRA fine-tuning, an iterative repair loop, and an RL stage; comparable RL work used a 32B model, suggesting the RL stage may dominate compute and be the binding constraint rather than the science.
practicality.question: Is the proposed pipeline feasible at reasonable compute?

practicality.finding: There is no evidence that Hits@1 on MetaQA 2-hop vs 3-hop is sensitive enough to attribute differences to supervision regime rather than to benchmark construction; a power/measurement check is needed.
practicality.question: Is the evaluation sensitive enough to detect the effect?

input.status_rationale: The idea is not refuted - the decisive experiment (training-time context supervision) has not been run and no directly matching prior work was found - but in its current form it is weak for three evidence-backed reasons. First, its central premise is directly challenged by the closest controlled evidence: non-answer-path triples contributed only +0.003 F1 at inference (C002) and inflated context introduces accuracy-depressing distractors (C003), so the expected effect is null or negative. Second, H2's premise has no direct support; the only RL transfer evidence is cross-formalism with a +1.7% downstream gain (C005). Third, the design is unidentifiable as stated because budget, answer-path presence, and format co-vary with the treatment (C007, C013). The gap is real and the direction is worth one careful, drastically narrowed experiment, but it needs the confounder controls, an inference-time context baseline, and a resolved passage-alignment definition before it can be called promising.

input.rationale: The challenged conclusion was H1's premise that same-passage surrounding context triples carry value for multi-hop KGQA. A controlled study holding triple count fixed found that replacing every non-answer-chain triple with unrelated-entity material changed accuracy by only +0.003 F1 (C002), and CLAUSE reports that inflated context introduces distractors that depress accuracy (C003). However, both are inference-time results, while the idea claims a training-time effect, so the premise is weakened by close analogy rather than refuted; no training-time experiment exists in the retrieved set. Verdict: weakened.

input.resolution: Partially resolved by the retrieved set: no directly matching work was found that uses same-passage context triples as a training-time supervision signal. All analyzed context-construction works (SG-RAG MOT, CLAUSE, Co-E, the answer-path prompt study) manipulate context at inference for an un-retrained reader, and the training-time works found (EmbedKGQA, GreaseLM, Variational Reasoning, STRuCT-LLM) do not use passage-context supervision. This is a search result over the recorded queries only; alternative terminology (e.g., contextualized KG pretraining, passage-grounded instruction tuning, graph-augmented LM pretraining) has not yet been searched.

The confounder is confirmed and now evidence-backed: a controlled study found non-answer-path triples contribute only +0.003 F1 while the answer chain carries most of the graph's value (C002), over-retrieval introduces distractors that depress accuracy (C003), and asymmetric prompt/format handling between context and no-context arms manufacturers spurious findings (C007). Mitigation required: matched token budget, identical templates except triple content, a shuffled/random-context arm, and a format-controlled scorer.

Still unvalidated. The only retrieved RL transfer evidence is cross-formalism (SQL training improving Cypher and vice versa) with a modest zero-shot downstream KGQA gain of +1.7% and no hop-depth analysis (C005). No analyzed paper trains only on lower-hop instances and measures accuracy transfer to deeper hops, so H2 remains a hypothesis requiring a pre-registered hop-depth experiment with a benchmark-construction check.

input.description: The planned comparison is triple-only training vs context-enriched training. But the field's strongest results come from inference-time context; the fair and decisive comparison is context-enriched training evaluated with the same inference-time context as a triple-only model, plus a training-free context baseline at matched budget. Comparing models that receive different context at test time conflates the training effect with the inference-context effect.
input.question: What is the correct control to isolate a training-time supervision effect from an inference-time context effect?
input.rationale: Given that inference-time context methods dominate the landscape and a training-free system is competitive with trained systems (C006), a supervision effect can only be claimed if the inference-time context is held constant or included as a factor.

input.description: The idea bundles three components (context-enriched supervision, adaptive one-hop repair loop, low-hop RL with deep-hop transfer). Given the challenge to H1 and the lack of support for H2, the direction may need to be narrowed to the single best-controlled question: does context-enriched supervision change multi-hop accuracy under matched budget and format, evaluated at the same inference context? The repair loop and RL stage may be premature scope.
input.question: Should the idea be narrowed to a single well-controlled supervision experiment before adding the repair loop and RL stages?
input.rationale: Each added component multiplies compute and confounds attribution; the critique found the core premise weak and the transfer claim unsupported, so running the full pipeline first would risk an uninterpretable result.
